# Redis command capability ledger

This report separates four claims that cannot be reduced to one coverage percentage: command-name availability, typed semantics, RESP wire support, and session/topology behavior. A typed name does not prove every option, reply shape, protocol form, or routing mode.

The machine-readable source is [`conformance/command-capabilities.json`](../conformance/command-capabilities.json). Unverified fields are explicit backlog, not implied support.

Logical ID: `command.blocking-dedicated`.

### Behavior session credential provider

Logical ID: `session.credential-provider`.

One shared credential provider backs fresh standalone and Cluster sockets plus dedicated Pub/Sub and MONITOR construction. Provider URL setup preserves transport, selected database and RESP negotiation; lookup, forced-refresh, transport and session setup can share one deadline. A forced-refresh failure is redacted and stops setup before SELECT, HELLO or application traffic. Established ordinary clients can reauthenticate through owned tasks with explicitly documented owner-specific failure retirement, while Pub/Sub reconnects with confirmed binary subscriptions and MONITOR terminates/reopens rather than accepting unsafe generic in-band AUTH. Provider errors and refresh-task tracing omit third-party error text and retain authentication classification.

- Dimensions: `session-ownership`, `reconnect`, `security`, `routing`
- Matrix: server `Redis 7.4.3 and 8.0.6 per-PR matrix plus deterministic provider/unit fixtures`; protocols `RESP2 setup, preserved RESP2/RESP3 URL negotiation`; features `core, URL/auth, Cluster, Pub/Sub, MONITOR, AWS and Entra providers`; topologies `standalone, cluster`

## Offline validation and refresh

Validate references, dispositions, source builders, pinned file hashes, and generated output without network access:

```bash
python3 scripts/generate_command_capabilities.py --check
python3 scripts/generate_command_coverage.py --check
```

To review a newer Redis documentation snapshot, fetch an explicit commit into a separate directory and compare it before changing provenance:

```bash
python3 scripts/fetch_command_metadata.py --ref <redis-docs-commit> \
  --output-dir /tmp/redis-command-metadata
python3 scripts/generate_command_capabilities.py \
  --compare-metadata /tmp/redis-command-metadata
```

The comparison reports added/removed names and any command-definition change, including scope, routing keys/flags, arity, versions, summaries, history, and arguments/options. Updating the five vendored files, their hashes, and every new disposition is a reviewed repository change. The downstream MCP project's [Redis 8.10.1 application ledger](https://github.com/redis-developer/redis-database-mcp-rs/blob/858a4dd84dfbc2102f80bdc18519e69afc47f263/docs/redis-command-coverage.md) has a different denominator and is not substituted for this client ledger.
